newsitem.title: UK: Fleming says shifted funds for business reasons.
newsitem.headline: Fleming says shifted funds for business reasons.

text.p: British investment bank Robert Fleming said on Sunday it had shifted the management of two investment funds to London from Hong Kong for business and personnel reasons earlier this year.

Reacting to Hong Kong and London reports that the bank had shifted management of more than 700 million pounds ($1.09 billion) of funds placed with its 50-percent-owned unit Jardine Fleming Investment Management (JFIM), a Robert Fleming spokesman said the move had been made early this year, in March or April.

The spokesman said the funds were moved as part of its strategy to build Asian market expertise and business in London and partly for personnel reasons after the departure from JFIM of fund manager Colin Armstrong.
Regulators in Hong Kong and London last week ordered compensation and fined Jardine Fleming over irregularities including front-running of trades, many involving Armstrong's personal account.

"It was a) business reasons and b) personnel reasons," said the Fleming spokesman of moving the funds, the Fleming Far Eastern Investment Trust and the Fleming Indian Investment Trust. "Firstly, Robert Fleming itself is a very big fund manager...and we need our own Asian expertise," said the spokesman.
Secondly, he said with the departure of Armstrong, promotions meant staff remaining did not have time left to run the trust.

The Sunday Telegraph newspaper in London highlighted the movement of the funds, saying this was a "sensitive time for Jardine which is engaged in a damage limitation exercise" following the regulators' moves last week.

A five-month probe by the Investment Regulatory Organisation (IMRO) in London and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) in Hong Kong exposed the late allocation of trades, and Jardine Fleming was fined 700,000 pounds.
Jardine Fleming is jointly owned by the Jardine Matheson and privately-owned Robert Fleming groups.
